### Risk Factors
- **Macro:** **NFP tomorrow at 07:30 CT is the single dominant variable** and today is the last full session in front of it. The book carries **84.50% deployment into a payrolls print** with a cyclical tilt (Materials + Industrials + Real Estate + Financials = 72.0% of deployed), which is the configuration most exposed to a hot print that reprices the rate path. That exposure is not a choice made today — it is the standing book — but it is the reason no further capital should be committed even if a slot somehow opened. Against it: every position carries a live GTC trailing stop, so the downside is mechanically bounded at 7–10% per name without any discretionary decision required.
- **Sector — Industrials:** **PH and HWM both report BMO**, and between Aerospace & Defence (~24% of XLI) and Machinery (~22%) they are the fund's two heaviest industries. **XLI is the book's second-best performer (+3.16%)** and a bad print from either is a direct markdown. This is the same shape of single-day idiosyncratic risk CAT posed on Aug 4, and it resolved benignly — which is not evidence it will again.
- **Sector — Health Care:** still the largest concentration at **27.98% of deployed across two names** (BIIB + XLV), though diluted from 30.17% by the XLF add. Neither reports today; the cluster risk is dormant this session but structurally unchanged, and **XLV's `rs10_negative_extended` reading is the first crack in what has been a +6.50pp RS50 leader** — worth watching rather than acting on.
- **Idiosyncratic — BIIB:** the only red name (−0.09%) and the only satellite. News flow is **constructive** — Q2 beat, FY26 adjusted-EPS guidance raised, RBC lifting its target to $242 (Outperform) against HSBC at $157 (Reduce), a genuinely split Street. The measured picture is better than the P&L implies: `rs10_positive`, **RS10 +1.50 / RS50 +3.14**, price above a rising 50-DMA ($201.44) and the 200-DMA ($184.28). Its Rule-16 decay chain **broke on Aug 5 (flag=0)** and today's marks do not re-arm it (10-session **+4.50% vs SPY +2.99%** — leading, not lagging), so the position is not rotation-eligible. The dated risk is unchanged: **IQLIK subcutaneous PDUFA Aug 24** and a guided **$290–320M Q3 acquired-IPR&D charge**.
- **Structural — the real cost of a full book:** deployment at 84.50% with 6/6 slots means **the portfolio can no longer respond to any opportunity without first freeing capital.** DELL screens at **RS50 +53.50pp** — far and away the strongest single-stock reading of the phase — and there is no mechanism to act on it before ~Aug 13 even if the calendar cleared, because both the slot and the headroom are spent. That is the deliberate trade-off yesterday's XLF entry made explicit ("any further add requires a Rule 8 scale-out or a Rule 16 rotation to free capital first"), and today is the first session where it binds. **Rule 16 offers no relief either — zero decay chains are armed** (all five Aug-5 flags returned flag=0), which is the book working well and simultaneously the reason nothing rotates out.
- **Marks and data quality:** oil feeds are stale, no fresh VIX print exists, and two positions report pre-market `change_today` of exactly 0.00. None of this changes today's decision — HOLD is forced by position count regardless of what any of those numbers say — but it would matter on a session where an entry were live, and it is recorded so the weekly review can see the pattern of feed staleness rather than infer a flat tape.

### Decision
**HOLD** — no orders, and for once the reasoning requires no judgment at all. **The book is 6/6 positions and 84.50% deployed with $51.07 of headroom; there is no legal entry available at any price, in any name, for any thesis.** This is the outcome yesterday's EOD snapshot predicted verbatim ("tomorrow's pre-market is overwhelmingly likely to be a HOLD by construction rather than by judgment"), and it is worth stating plainly that this is the *good* kind of forced HOLD: the constraint binds because capital is fully and deliberately deployed into the four best-measured sectors in the complex (XLF +8.55pp, XLV +6.50, XLI +5.25, XLB +1.56 — four of the top five), not because opportunity is absent. Five of six positions are green, all six carry live GTC trailing stops, zero decay chains are armed, and the weekly buy budget sits at 2/5 with three unused — the book is doing exactly what v3 asks of it going into a payrolls print. **The one thing worth carrying forward is DELL:** `rs10_positive` with **RS50 +53.50pp**, above a rising 50-DMA and a 200-DMA it more than doubled, it is the strongest single-stock screen result of the phase and it is unbuyable today on three separate gates. It replaces GS at the top of the **~Aug 13 satellite watchlist** (DELL > GS > FFIV), by which date CPI and PPI will have cleared and a Rule 8 scale-out or Rule 16 rotation may have freed the slot it needs. Until then: hold, let the trails do the work, and let tomorrow's NFP resolve into a book that is already positioned rather than one still deciding. Patience > activity — today it is also the only option the rulebook permits.

### Risk Factors
- **Macro — the payrolls print is today, not tomorrow.** Consensus ~91k / 4.3%. The book carries **84.36% deployment and a 72.01%-of-deployed cyclical tilt** (Materials + Real Estate + Industrials + Financials) into an 08:30 ET Tier-1 binary, which is the configuration most exposed to a hot print that reprices the rate path — Financials would benefit, Real Estate would be hit hardest, and XLRE is 23.95% of deployed. That exposure is the standing book, not a decision made today, and it is mechanically bounded: **every position carries a live GTC trailing stop at 7–10%**, so no discretionary decision is required in any scenario. It is also the reason no capital should be committed even if a slot opened at 09:00.
- **Rule 16 — two decay chains are live and both are on track to fire at midday.** This is the single most consequential item today. **BIIB (flag=1 as of Aug 6)** is **−1.40% below entry** on this morning's mark and lagging SPY over 10 sessions (**RS10 −1.29pp**); **XLF (flag=1)** is **−0.74% below entry** and lagging (**RS10 −0.57pp**). If both conditions hold at the midday check, **both arm flag=2 and become ROTATE-EXIT candidates in the same session** — which would take the book from 6/6 to 4/6 and free roughly $2,005 of headroom in a single afternoon. Two observations follow. First, the losses are shallow (−1.40% and −0.74%, nowhere near the Rule 7 −7% line), so this would be a *momentum* exit, not a damaged-thesis exit — exactly what Rule 16 was written for, and exactly the case where it feels premature. Second, **XLF measures RS50 +9.23pp, the strongest medium-term reading of all eleven sectors**, and would be rotated out on a 10-session lag against a benchmark that itself ran +4.12% in those ten sessions. That is a real tension between the two arms of the rulebook and it should be named for the weekly review rather than resolved here by discretion — **midday runs the deterministic check and midday decides.** A green tape after the payrolls print breaks both chains.
- **Sector — Health Care remains the largest cluster** at **27.99% of deployed across two names** (BIIB + XLV). Neither reports today. XLV's RS50 +8.56pp is second-best in the complex, so the cluster is well-positioned on measurement; the concentration risk is structural rather than event-driven this session.
- **Idiosyncratic — BIIB.** News flow is **constructive on fundamentals**: the **RayThera acquisition closed Aug 6** (immunology small-molecule pipeline), Q2 revenue $2.74B / adj EPS $3.60 beat, FY26 guidance raised to mid-single-digit revenue growth. Measurement is the problem, not the story — `constructive_pullback`, RS50 +4.18pp, above a rising 50-DMA $201.70 and a 200-DMA $184.59, but RS10 −1.29 and below entry, which is what has the decay chain armed.
- **Structural — the week's buy budget expires unused.** Three of five Week-15 trades remain and today is the last session of the week; they cannot be carried. The book has now closed **seven consecutive sessions unchanged in composition**, and the binding constraint has been the position cap, not the budget — which is the argument the weekly review should take up this afternoon: whether a 6-position cap plus an 85% deployment ceiling leaves any room for the 5-trade weekly cap to mean anything.

None of this changes today's decision — HOLD is forced by position count regardless — but the pattern is now persistent enough to belong in the weekly review rather than in a per-day caveat.

### Decision
**HOLD** — no orders. As yesterday, the reasoning requires no judgment: **the book is 6/6 positions and 84.36% deployed with $65.05 of headroom against a $510.89 minimum clip; there is no legal entry available at any price, in any name, for any thesis.** What is different today is *why* that is worth recording. The macro-window — the gate that blocked the entire satellite sleeve for seven straight sessions — **cleared overnight**, and it cleared into a one-session-wide opening (CPI puts T+2 back in force from Monday). So for the first time in the phase, the constraint set is purely mechanical: no calendar excuse, just a full book. And even had a slot existed, **the screen would have refused every candidate anyway** — MU, TXN, HWKN, PPC fail on RS50; NTRS, GS, DELL fail on RS10; not one unheld sector ETF passes. **Zero of nine satellite candidates and zero of six unheld sectors are buyable on merit**, which makes today the rare session where the caps and the screen agree rather than one masking the other. That agreement is the useful signal: SPY ran **+4.12% in ten sessions** and the leadership that produced it is not in anything this book could add. The one live variable is **Rule 16 — BIIB and XLF both carry armed decay chains into midday**, and if both fire the book goes to 4/6 with ~$2,005 freed, which would be the first genuine change in composition in seven sessions. That decision belongs to the deterministic midday check, not to this routine. Until then: hold into payrolls, let the six trails bound the downside, and let **the Friday 16:00 CT weekly review** take up the two structural questions this week surfaced — the unusable-VIX feed, and whether a 5-trade weekly cap can mean anything under a 6-position cap and an 85% ceiling. Patience > activity — today it is again the only option the rulebook permits.

### Decision
**HOLD** — no orders. **The reasoning is different from the last eight sessions and that difference is the point of this entry.** Every mechanical gate that has forced HOLD since Jul 29 is now open: the book is **4/6 with two free slots**, the satellite sleeve is **0/3 with all three free**, cash is **$3,617**, headroom is **$2,077** against a **$513** minimum clip, and the weekly budget is **0/5 on a fresh week**. For the first time in the phase there is nothing structural stopping a buy. What stops it is the **deterministic screen: 0 of 11 sector ETFs pass `rscreen`, and the 2 single stocks that do pass — CRDO (RS10 +12.59 / RS50 +9.65) and FERG (+6.63 / +8.40) — are blocked by Rule v3.2 because CPI sits at exactly T+2.** So today is the mirror image of Friday: then, the calendar cleared into a full book; now, the book has cleared into a closed calendar. Both are the rulebook operating as designed, and neither is a defect to override from here.

Two things are worth stating without hedging. First, **the cost is real and it is compounding**: 64.77% deployed is a second session below the floor, Week 15 already measured −1.78pp from this exact mechanism, and the v3.4 re-deployment trigger — which arms tomorrow — **cannot fix it**, because it relaxes R:R and the binding constraint is the RS screen. That is a v3.4 gap, not a v3.4 success, and Friday's review should treat it as one. Second, **the screen may be right anyway**: SPY ran +4.65% in ten sessions and the leadership producing that is in nothing this book can legally add — XLK and XLY are the only positive-RS10 sectors and both fail RS50, which is precisely the "buy the market-tracker at the top" trade the Week-14 review named as the phase's worst habit.

So: hold, let the four trails bound the downside into Wednesday's CPI, and treat **CRDO and DELL as the live watchlist for the Thu Aug 13 / Fri Aug 14 window** when the macro gate reopens. The one variable today is **SPG after the close**, which is the most likely trigger for an XLRE decay chain at Tuesday's midday — a deterministic check, not a discretionary one. Patience > activity — but today, for the first time, patience is a screen's verdict rather than a cap's arithmetic, and that is a materially more informative kind of HOLD.

### Risk Factors
- **Macro — CPI at T+1, and the core exemption is doing real work today.** The v3.2 macro-window gate exempts core ETFs by design, so XLI is proposable into a binary that vetoes seven satellites. That asymmetry is intentional (a diversified sector ETF is not a single-name event bet) but **today is the first session where the Rule 5 relaxed floor and the core exemption combine to admit a trade the book would otherwise not take**, and it deserves to be read that way on Friday rather than absorbed silently. A hot CPI hits cyclicals and rate-sensitives together — XLI, XLRE and XLB are all on the wrong side of that print.
- **Macro — the two dominant narratives contradict each other.** Soft payrolls (-23k) argue for cuts; **oil +5% on Iran/Hormuz** argues for stickier headline inflation. They cannot both be right into tomorrow's number, and the position that resolves them is CPI itself. VIX at 15.46 is not pricing much of either.

### Risk Factors
- **Macro — CPI at T+0, and the core exemption is again the only reason a trade is proposable.** The v3.2 macro-window gate exempts core ETFs by design, so XLE is proposable into a binary that vetoes the entire satellite sleeve. Today the asymmetry is **less uncomfortable than yesterday's**, and for a specific reason: XLI, XLB and XLRE are all on the losing side of a hot print (rates channel), whereas **XLE is on the side that a hot print would most likely be reporting** — energy is the component the Hormuz premium feeds into. This is the first proposed idea of the phase whose macro exposure runs *counter* to the book's, rather than doubling it.
- **Macro — a soft CPI is the risk to this idea, not a hot one.** The inverse of the above: a benign print that rallies the tape broadly would likely coincide with the geopolitical premium deflating, and XLE is the book's only name that depends on that premium holding. **The Hormuz story is two sessions old and priced; it is not a fresh catalyst.**
- **Idiosyncratic — XLE is extended and the screen's primary arm does not test for it.** Price sits **+7.56% above its 50-DMA** and **within 3.4% of its 52-week high ($63.01)**. Yesterday XLB was rejected from the *constructive-pullback* exception at 3.83% of extension, but `rs10_positive` — the arm XLE clears — carries **no extension test at all**. That is the screen as designed, not a bug, but it means **today's pass is a momentum-chase pass, and the 9-share sizing is the mitigant**. A full-size clip here would not be defensible.
- **XLRE — the Rule 16 chain runs into a third midday, and branch 1 is still undefined.** Today's readings have **deteriorated, not healed**: RS10 **-8.20pp** (from -6.9pp), RS50 **-1.05pp**, and price has now **fallen below its 50-DMA** ($44.08 vs $44.64) for the first time in the chain. SPY's 10-session return is **+4.01%**, still above the +3.0% melt-up threshold, and the position is **-1.70%** vs entry, still shallower than the -2.0% floor — so the guard will most likely **suppress for a second consecutive session**. **Read midday's actual `sizing.py decay` output rather than assuming this preview.** The structural point stands unchanged and is Friday's top item: the sector-quadrant override is the only path that can release the guard, its test has **no operational definition**, and XLRE has now lost its 50-DMA while the book holds it on that undefined discretion.
- **Structural — Rule 5's restore budget has fallen below the minimum-position floor, which is a new failure mode.** With restore at **$491.68** and the 5% floor at **$513.20**, the trigger can no longer size a *compliant* clip at its own mandate; every restoring trade must now overshoot the budget to be legal. This is the **fourth consecutive session** on which the redeploy trigger's arming has not been the binding constraint — `rscreen` and Rule 3 were the blockers, and now the floor is. **Carry to Friday: the trigger needs either a floor-aware clamp or an explicit "overshoot to floor" allowance, because as written the two rules contradict each other whenever the gap to the band is under 5% of equity.**
- **Concentration — XLB is over the Rule 3 cap on appreciation.** XLB at **20.77%** of equity (from 20.74% Tuesday) is above the 20% cap purely on gains — **not a breach, but frozen: it may not be added to**, and it continues to drift further out as it rallies. XLI at **19.93%** is at the cap by construction. Together the two cyclicals are **40.70%** of equity and **58.0% of deployed**, correlated through the same rates/growth channel even though GICS treats them as separate sectors.
- **`replace-stop` hwm reset — unresolved, carried from Tuesday.** Tightening a trail via `replace-stop` resets the trailing high-water mark to the current price rather than carrying the old one (XLB $53.595 → $53.085, XLV $169.66 → $167.86 on Aug 11). Harmless when a name is near its high; on a name that has run far above its current print, a *tighter* trail could produce a *lower* effective stop. Rule 9 verifies `stop_price` so it would catch the breach, but the ladder would be silently surrendering earned protection. **Friday review item.**

### Decision
**TRADE** — one idea: `pm-2026-08-12-XLE`, 9 shares, ~$548.

Three things had to be simultaneously true for anything to pass today, and they were: the Rule 5 trigger is armed (fifth session below the floor), a core ETF cleared `rscreen` outright rather than by exception, and the sector ledger does not bar it. **XLE is the first `rs10_positive` core pass of the phase** — every prior core entry, including Tuesday's XLI, came through the constructive-pullback door. It is also the book's first genuine macro hedge: four held names all lose on a hot CPI, and this one does not.

It is a **small, deliberately under-sized, cap-and-floor-bounded opener**, not a conviction clip, and it is under-sized precisely because the name is extended and the screen's primary arm does not test extension. **It does not fix deployment either** — 75.55% is inside the band by 0.55pp, and the book needs the satellite sleeve (Fri Aug 14) or an XLB/XLRE exit to sit comfortably. Patience > activity; but the screen passed on its own terms, and that is what the screen is for.

### Risk Factors
- **Macro — PPI is T+0 and prints 69 minutes before this routine's successor runs.** The rule permits it and the sequencing is favourable (entry after the print, not before), but "favourable sequencing" is not "no risk": a hot PPI hits at 07:30 CT and `market-open` will size FERG at 08:39 CT into whatever tape that leaves. **Industrials are directly exposed** — producer prices are an input cost line for a distribution business, and FERG's margin story is the thesis. **`market-open` must re-derive the entry off live marks and re-run `rscreen` if the print moves the name more than ~2%**; a limit order struck at yesterday's $245.18 into a gap is the failure mode. The book's other three cyclicals (XLB, XLI, XLRE) are on the same side of the print.
- **Concentration — this is the largest single-name position the book has ever proposed.** FERG at **14.33% of equity** is roughly 2.7× the average satellite clip and is the direct consequence of risk-parity sizing meeting a 13% stop with $1,517.84 of headroom to absorb it. It is legal (≤20% Rule 3, ≤50% sector) and it is what the sizer returns, but it should be read as what it is: **five weeks of an empty satellite sleeve resolving into one concentrated bet, on the one day the calendar allowed it.** If FERG gaps through $213.31 the book loses ~1.9% of equity in a single name.
- **Idiosyncratic — FERG's 50-DMA is below its 200-DMA.** Covered in the idea, restated here because it is the strongest argument against the trade: the checklist tests *price* against both averages and FERG clears, but the **averages themselves are still in the wrong order**, which is a base recovering rather than a trend extending. The 13% stop sits **10.9% below the 200-DMA** — a full failure of the recovery would be a long, slow bleed rather than a fast stop-out. The mitigants are the dated catalyst, the passed earnings, and the 3.5-ATR stop; they do not make the structure clean.
- **Structural — the `rs10_positive` arm has no extension test, and today that gap did the screening work.** Six candidates passed the screen at **12.8% to 27.8%** above their own 50-DMAs. The deterministic screen approved all six; only judgment rejected them. That is the wrong division of labour for a rulebook whose whole point is that verdicts are not reached by eye. **Concretely proposable fix for Friday: apply the `constructive_pullback` band's spirit to the primary arm — reject `rs10_positive` above some extension ceiling (a 3× ATR14 band would cut all six and keep FERG at +4.45% and NTRS at +6.99%).** Logging the numbers here so Friday has evidence rather than an impression.
- **Structural — the Rule 5 floor-vs-restore contradiction is untouched.** `redeploy --equity 10265.48 --lmv 7207.82 --sessions-below-band 4` → `{"triggered": true, "rr_floor": 1.5, "restore_dollars": 491.29}`, against a 5%-of-equity minimum clip of **$513.27**. The restore budget is **$21.98 short of the smallest position the sizer will build**, so **any** `rr-relaxed` core ballast add today returns `floor_skip` exactly as XLE did. **Today's trade routes around the contradiction; it does not resolve it.** FERG escapes only because a 2:1 satellite is exempt from the clamp by construction. **Friday's top item, unchanged and now one session more overdue.**
- **XLRE — the Rule 16 chain runs into a fourth midday and the readings have deteriorated again.** RS10 **-9.10pp** (from -8.20pp), RS50 **+1.63pp**, price **-0.40% below** its 50-DMA. SPY's 10-session return has risen to **+5.90%**, far above the +3.0% melt-up threshold, and the position is **-0.67%** vs entry, shallower than the -2.0% floor → the guard will most likely **suppress for a third consecutive session**. Preview only: **read midday's actual `sizing.py decay` output.** The structural gap is unchanged — branch 1's "exited the leading momentum quadrant" test still has **no operational definition** and is still the only path that can release the guard.
- **Stale pre-market quotes on both candidates.** `alpaca.sh quote FERG` returns **ask $0.00** with a 20:00 UTC timestamp; `quote NTRS` returns **bid $178.12 / ask $200.72**, an 11% artifact. Neither is a live spread — both are post-close book snapshots. **All liquidity judgments in this entry rest on 20-day average dollar volume from the bar pulls, not on those quotes**, and `market-open` must engage its stale-quote fallback rather than pricing off them.
- **Oil is unwinding and the book has no Energy exposure — which is now a *relative* miss, not a risk.** WTI -2% and Brent -1.8% as the Hormuz premium deflates. The book owns no XLE, so there is no direct hit; the point is that **yesterday's rejected idea would have been bought into the top of a two-day spike**, and the mechanism that prevented it was a bug, not a rule.
- **Sector — Industrials becomes the book's largest sleeve.** Post-fill, Industrials (XLI $2,044.68 + FERG $1,471.08) = **40.51% of deployed**, against a 50% cap. Adding a *second* Industrials satellite would breach the spirit of the diversification rule well before it breaches the number, so **HWM, UAL and APG should be treated as unavailable for the rest of the week** if FERG fills.

### Decision
**TRADE** — one idea: `pm-2026-08-13-FERG`, 6 shares, ~$1,471. `pm-2026-08-13-NTRS` is the runner-up and is expected to `floor_skip` on exhausted headroom.

The satellite sleeve has been empty for **five consecutive weeks**, and for the last three of those the block was the calendar rather than the screen. **Today the calendar cleared** — CPI resolved in line and produced no dislocation, PPI is T+0 and resolves before entry, and T+1/T+2 are both empty for the first time since mid-July. Two names clear the screen on its **primary arm** while remaining un-extended, and one of them carries a **dated earnings beat, three target raises, no earnings event inside the hold window, and $1B/day of liquidity**.

It is also the only trade available. **Both core passes are barred by other rules**, and every `rr-relaxed` core add is `floor_skip`ped by the unresolved Rule 5 contradiction. A 2:1 satellite is the single instrument that reaches the full headroom, and filling it puts deployment at **84.54% — back inside the Rule 5 band for the first time in six sessions**, which nothing else on the board can do.

The honest counterweight: this is the book's **largest single-name position ever proposed** (14.33%), into a name whose 50-DMA is still below its 200-DMA, on the day of a producer-price print that bears directly on its margin thesis. Those are real and they are why the stop is 13% rather than 15% and why `market-open` is instructed to re-price off live marks. But patience is a bias toward *not acting when nothing passes* — and after five weeks of nothing passing, something passed on the primary arm, with a catalyst that is dated rather than narrated.

**Three independent gates bind simultaneously, and any one of them alone would produce the same answer:**
1. **Deployment ceiling** — $36.71 of headroom, `floor_skip` on every clip at any price on the board.
2. **Rule 3 drift** — the three core names the screen passed or would favour (XLB 20.22%, XLRE 20.11%, XLI 19.87%) are at or through the 20% cap on appreciation. **The one slot free in the position count cannot be filled by anything the core screen likes.**
3. **Merit** — the four passing satellites are 11.5–19.3% extended; the one that is not (FERG) is already held.

**This is the mirror image of the week's earlier complaint and deserves to be logged as such.** Monday through Wednesday the indictment was that Rule 5's restore mechanism was self-blocking — `triggered: true` for three sessions, `acted: false` for two, because the restore budget kept opening below the minimum clip. Today the *same arithmetic* produces the opposite failure: the book is at the top of the band, and the identical `floor_skip` clamp now prevents deploying the three unused buy slots that expire at today's close. **In both regimes the minimum-clip floor is what refuses the trade, and in neither does anything downstream notice.** Week 16 will close **2/5 on the buy budget** not because five ideas failed screening but because the sizing floor and the deployment ceiling leave no gap between them wide enough for a position to exist. **That is the second item for today's review, and it is now better evidenced than when it was only a low-deployment problem.**

*(For `market-open`: nothing is proposed and nothing should be bought. Headroom is recomputed on live state at ~08:39 CT, and the ratio is sticky — cash is only 15.36%, so restoring a $516 clip requires LMV to fall roughly 5% relative to equity. If a gap-down somehow opens that much room, **ANET remains the only name that is both fresh and sector-additive** — Info Tech, a sector this book has zero exposure to — but it enters at +17.4% extension and should be treated as a watch item, not a queued order.)*

### Risk Factors
- **Macro:** July retail sales at 07:30 CT is the month's largest consumer read and lands **before** `market-open` runs — a downside surprise would hit the cyclical core (XLI, XLB, 64.7% of deployed between them) hardest. UMich prelim at 09:00 CT lands *after*. Neither is Tier-1 for the macro-window gate, and with nothing to buy the routine has no exposure to either print beyond what it already holds.
- **Positioning:** **deployment 84.64% is 0.36pp from the ceiling with 15.36% cash** — the book is as fully invested as the rules allow, which is the right place to be in a rallying tape but leaves **no dry powder for a Monday dislocation** and no capacity to act on the FOMC minutes at T+3.
- **Concentration:** Industrials **40.82% of deployed** across XLI and FERG. Below the 50% cap, but a single sector shock now moves two-fifths of the book, and three of five names (XLB, XLI, XLRE) sit within 0.2pp of the 20% per-position cap.
- **Breadth:** premarket is **Nasdaq +1.30% vs Dow +0.05%** — a narrow, tech-led bid into a book with **zero Technology exposure**. The likely shape of today is a green index and negative daily alpha for a third consecutive session, from sector composition rather than from anything going wrong. That is a real cost and the honest reason the empty Tech sleeve keeps appearing in these entries.
- **Complacency:** VIX 14.62 at the floor of its 52-week range for a third session, after two Tier-1 prints resolved benign. Cheap protection, and nothing in the book is buying it.
- **Idiosyncratic:** FERG priced **$1.2bn of senior notes** ($700m 4.800% due 2029, $500m 5.600% due 2036) closing **today**, funding the FWI Holdings acquisition; ex-dividend approaches with an **Aug 21 record date** for the $0.89 quarterly. Both are known, financing-related and already in the price — FERG is **+3.03% in two sessions** and its 10% trail sits $29.42 below. No action implied.
- **Screen-source caveat:** the momentum query returns earnings-revision leaders, which this session correlate **negatively** with price relative strength (6 of 7 fail `rs50_negative`). Treat it as an idea generator whose output must clear `rscreen`, never as a ranking.

### Decision
**HOLD.** No orders. Zero ideas pass the buy-side gate — deployment headroom of $36.71 `floor_skip`s every clip, the three cap-adjacent core names cannot absorb an add, and the four satellites that pass `rscreen` are 11.5–19.3% extended. Positions stay 5/6 with all five names green and all five protected by GTC trails; Week 16 closes 2/5 on the buy budget. Patience > activity — and today patience is not a preference but the only legal move.

### Risk Factors
- **Macro — the FOMC minutes at T+1 are the week's only Tier-1 print, and the book is fully invested into them.** Deployment 84.60% with 15.40% cash means there is **no dry powder to act on the release in either direction**, and no capacity to add on a dislocation. The gate correctly stops new satellite risk from being taken *into* the event; it does nothing about the risk already held. Sources also disagree on whether the release is Tue Aug 18 or Wed Aug 19 — treat both sessions as event days.
- **Macro — oil is re-inflating on the third pass of the Hormuz story.** WTI +0.9% / Brent +1.1%, both >10% off last week's lows on stalled reopening talks, with one source pointing at $100 Brent. A genuine energy shock is inflationary and would hit the cyclical core hardest — **XLI + XLB are 64.6% of deployed** — while rate-sensitive **XLRE (23.91%)** takes the second-order hit through yields. The book holds **zero Energy**, so there is no offset. Against that: the story has spiked and fully deflated twice in two weeks and oil is still below April levels, so this is a *known* risk being re-priced, not a new one.
- **Positioning — 0.40pp from the ceiling with three of five names through the per-position cap.** The book is as fully invested as the rules allow, which is the right place to be in a rallying tape, but it leaves no room to express any view for a fifth session and no capacity to rotate without first selling something.
- **Concentration — Industrials 40.50% of deployed** across XLI and FERG. Below the 50% cap, but a single sector shock moves two-fifths of the book, and XLB / XLI / XLRE all sit within 0.5pp of the 20% per-position cap.
- **Breadth / composition — the empty Technology sleeve is now a measurable drag, and the honest cost of the rules.** XLK's 10-session RS is **+4.44pp**, the best on the sector board, while its RS50 (-6.25pp) and falling 50-DMA keep it `pass=0`. AI/semiconductor leadership is the tape's stated driver and the book has **zero exposure**. Expect green-index / negative-alpha sessions to keep recurring from sector composition rather than from anything going wrong.
- **Complacency — VIX 14.92 at the floor of a 13.38–35.30 range for a fourth session**, and *up* 4.7% against +0.68% futures. Cheap protection ahead of the only Tier-1 print of the week, and nothing in the book is buying it.
- **Idiosyncratic — FERG.** The $1.2bn senior-notes issue (Q2 FY26 beat, FY26 revenue guidance raised to mid-single-digit growth, CapEx guidance lifted to $375–425m) closed Friday; the **$0.89 quarterly dividend has an Aug 21 record date**, so the ex-date falls inside this week and will mechanically clip the price. Sources disagree on the worst S&P sector by 25pp because they cite different cutoff dates; one puts Info Tech at +22.3% YTD and another at -2.92%. Every sector verdict in this entry comes from `alpaca.sh bars`.

**HOLD.** No orders — and this routine placed none of any kind, including no `trailing-stop` (Rules 17 and 18 both clean). Zero ideas pass the buy-side gate: **$41.43 of headroom `floor_skip`s every clip** ($473.38 short of the $514.81 minimum), **FOMC minutes at T+1 macro-gate all four passing satellites**, and **Rule 3 drift blocks the only core name the screen likes** (XLRE, held at 20.23%). A repeat deflation is a **direct XLE risk** — which is the position the sizing clamp has kept the book out of three times — and an indirect XLB/XLI input cost tailwind on the way down.
- **Sector, XLRE:** **AVB's S&P 500 deletion at today's open** removes index demand from the book's flattest name on the day its RS50 turned negative. Two adverse inputs converging on one 20.11% position, protected only by a 10% trail that sits **6.7% below** the current mark.

- **Structural, sixth session:** 84.54% deployed with **$47.38** of legal headroom means the book **cannot respond to any signal it generates**, good or bad, on the buy side. Three of five names are at or through the Rule 3 cap. The only mechanisms that can free capital are a stop firing, a Rule 8 scale-out or a Rule 16 rotation — i.e. **the book can currently only act by selling.** This is the third consecutive session logging it and it is now the top structural item for Friday's review, alongside the still-undefined Branch 1 quadrant test (DECIDED-G, twelve middays).

**HOLD.** Zero trade ideas. Three constraints, each independently sufficient: **(1) capital** — $47.38 headroom vs a $512.82 minimum clip, `floor_skip` on both live core passes; **(2) macro-window** — FOMC minutes T+1 vetoes the entire satellite sleeve including its one screen pass; **(3) per-name** — of four core passes, XLI is capped, XLP is sector-barred, XLE is a chase at +9.86% extension, and XLV fails only on (1). ### Rule 16 — FERG's decay chain is live and would rotate today *(midday owns the decision)*
Yesterday's midday logged **`flag=1, rotate=0`** — the phase's first non-zero decay flag. On pre-open data the second link is in place: `sizing.py decay --unrealized-pct -0.338 --pos-ret-10d -4.32 --spy-ret-10d -0.50 --prior-flag 1` → **`{"flag": 1, "rotate": 1, "suppressed": 0, "reason": "rotate"}`**.

**What matters for planning:** a FERG rotation frees **~$1,467**, which is **28× the current $52.17 of headroom** and would end the capital bind that has produced six consecutive HOLDs. **If it fires, tomorrow's first call is XLV** (only name failing on capital alone, 9.97pp of Rule 3 room), **with XLF second** on volatility-adjusted terms. - **Structural, and the single most consequential thing in the book today: XLI's armed Rule 16 chain.** XLI closed yesterday at `flag=1` (below entry, 10-session -2.12% vs SPY). **A second flag at today's midday rotates a core ETF out — the first time Rule 16 has ever threatened the core sleeve** — freeing ~$2,000 and dropping deployment straight back to ~59%, undoing the band restoration this idea achieves. **DE reports before the open and is an Industrials bellwether**, so today's print is a live input into that decision. ### Decision
**TRADE — 1 idea, `pm-2026-08-20-XLV`, 7 shares, ~$1,229.76.**

First TRADE decision since Aug 13 and the end of a four-session HOLD run. **The reason for the change is not a new signal but the removal of the constraint that suppressed the old one:** XLV has been the log's "standing first call the moment headroom appears" for three consecutive sessions, blocked each time by `floor_skip` at $41–52 of headroom. Yesterday's Rule 16 rotation and Rule 8 scale-out freed **$1,815.12**; headroom is now **$1,860.10**, and the same name that failed on capital alone now sizes to a legal 7-share clip on the first pass. **It also fixes the problem that freeing the capital created** — deployment at **66.89%** is below the Rule 5 floor, and this add restores the band to **78.86%** without needing the 1.5:1 relaxation that would arm tomorrow.

**Stated against itself:** the entry is late and extended (+9.25%, 5.4 ATRs), and this entry says so in the same breath it proposes the trade. The judgement is that **best-in-complex leadership on both RS windows, in the least-concentrated sleeve, on the lowest ATR of any passing name, with a resolved rather than pending catalyst**, is worth a poor entry price when the alternative is a fifth consecutive HOLD at 67% deployed — which is the exact configuration Rule 5's v3.4 amendment was written to stop, at a measured cost of **-1.78pp in Week 15**.

**No exits proposed and no stops moved** — this routine places none. **XLI's second decay flag and XLRE's continued RS decay are both handed to midday, which owns them**, with the explicit note that a Rule 16 rotation of XLI this afternoon would reverse today's deployment gain.

### Risk Factors
- **Macro:** Tape is flat-to-lower into a Tier-1-empty session; the real macro risk sits at **T+3 (July PCE, Aug 26)** and **T+4–6 (Jackson Hole, Aug 27–29)**, both outside the satellite entry window by design but both inside the *holding* window. A hawkish Jackson Hole would hit a 75%-deployed book with no protection and a 15.7 VIX offering none.
- **Oil / geopolitical:** Brent $93+ is a **stalled-Hormuz premium**, not a demand signal. It cuts both ways — a resolution headline unwinds Energy violently (which is why XLE and XOM/CVX/COP are refused), while an escalation is an input-cost shock to the Materials sleeve the book is already 34.7% deployed into.
- **Sector / idiosyncratic — the largest sleeve is the weakest link.** **XLB is the book's biggest position (20.61% of equity), its RS50 just went negative (−0.09pp), one vendor calls Materials "extremely overbought," and the copper squeeze that underwrote much of the move just cracked** (backwardation $545 → $248 on Trafigura LME deliveries). XLB carries a 5% trail so the downside is bounded, but this is the position most likely to be the next Rule 16 or Rule 8 event.
- **Concentration if idea #1 fills:** Health Care goes to **45.36% of deployed** — inside the 50% cap but the tightest it has been, and it means XLV and GILD share a sector-level shock. Deliberate: it is where the measured relative strength is (XLV RS50 +8.29pp, GILD +11.31pp), but it is a single-sector bet on two instruments.
- **GILD idiosyncratic:** the Q2 print carried a **GAAP diluted loss of −$8.45 and non-GAAP −$6.75** on acquired-IPR&D and tax charges. The guidance raise and the franchise growth are the thesis; a market that re-fixates on the headline loss line is the bear case. Also, one August note (RBC, $123) sits **below** the current price — the $158.04 consensus is an average over a genuinely wide dispersion.
- **Deployment:** even after a fill the book is at 74.75% — **still fractionally under the floor**. If the fill misses, this is the fourth sub-floor session and the cash drag compounds into a weekend.
- **Data quality:** YTD sector-performance vendors disagreed by ~20pp on Energy (+22–26% vs +44.6%). Only the `bars`-derived RS table was used for any decision.

### Trade Ideas
**None.** Zero ideas cleared the buy-side gate, so no numbered lines are written. The two closest are documented above with their arithmetic: **XLF** (fails 2:1 by requiring a +20.0% target vs Friday's +15.0%) and **XLE** (fails 2:1 by requiring a +9.0% mark-up of its own standing target). Neither is a conviction failure; both are ratio failures at a floor that moved against them over the weekend.

**A structural note for Friday's review, and the real finding of this run.** With the **canonical 10% trail** that `daily-summary` places on every position (36 placements, zero exceptions), a **2:1** R:R requires a **+20% target**. No sector ETF supports a +20% target honestly — there is no analyst range to anchor one, and a 20% sector move is a quarter's work, not a swing. The consequence is mechanical: **`tier: core` adds are effectively only possible while Rule 5's relaxed 1.5:1 floor (a +15% target) is armed — and Rule 5 only arms *after* the book has already spent two sessions below the deployment floor.** The rule that exists to restore ballast can therefore only fire once the ballast is already gone. Today is the clean demonstration: the book is in band, has two free slots, $1,027 of ceiling headroom and a sector (Financials) that just flipped to outright RS leadership — and the gate that stops it is a floor that would have permitted the same purchase 24 hours earlier. **This is not a rule violation and was not overridden; it is a proposal for the review.**

### Risk Factors
- **Macro — the week is back-loaded and the book is fully invested into it.** **July PCE Wed Aug 26 (T+2)** then **Powell at Jackson Hole Thu Aug 27 (T+3)**, into a **75.07%-deployed** book with **no protection** and a **15.9 VIX** offering none cheaply. A hot PCE print followed by a hawkish Jackson Hole is the adverse path, and it hits **Real Estate (26.71% of deployed) hardest** — the single most rate-sensitive sleeve in the book, already the weakest name on RS (XLRE RS50 −4.75pp, deteriorating from −2.61pp Friday).
- **NVIDIA earnings this week are an index-level event the book cannot express a view on.** Zero Info Tech exposure means a beat costs the book relative alpha on a day SPY rallies, and a miss protects it. This is a **deliberate** consequence of XLK screening `pass=0 rs50_negative`, but it is a real source of tracking error in either direction, and it lands in the same 72 hours as PCE and Jackson Hole.
- **Oil reversal is live, not hypothetical.** Both benchmarks are **down 1.5–2.2% this morning on profit-taking ahead of an Iran-sanctions announcement**, after a sharp weekly rally. The book holds no Energy, so the direct exposure is nil — but this is the first hard evidence for the mechanic that has refused XLE six times, and it cuts the other way for **Materials (27.72% of deployed)**, where lower input costs are a mild positive.
- **Concentration — Health Care at 45.57% of deployed is the tightest single-sector bet of the phase**, expressed through two instruments (XLV core + GILD satellite) that share a policy and pipeline-sentiment shock. Inside the 50% cap, deliberate, and sited where the measured RS is (XLV RS50 +8.92pp, GILD +15.25pp) — but it leaves only **$687.58** of sector room and means one adverse HC headline moves ~46% of the invested book.
- **Rule 3 drift, twelfth session:** **XLB 20.81%** and **XLRE 20.05%** of equity sit *through* the 20% per-position cap on appreciation. Not a breach — neither was bought through it — but neither can absorb a share, and it is the reason today's screening had to look for a *new* name rather than an add. XLRE crossing back above 20% is new as of today.
- **Idiosyncratic — XLRE is the standing weak link and it got weaker.** RS50 deteriorated **−2.61pp → −4.75pp** over one session, it is the **thinnest** ETF in the complex ($251M/day), it sits at **+0.65%** unrealized after 40 sessions, and it faces the week's rate risk most directly. The two closest are documented above with their arithmetic: **XLF** (2:1 requires a +20.0% target vs the +15.0% derived Friday) and **XLE** (2:1 requires an +8.1% mark-up of its own Aug 12 target). Neither is a conviction failure; both are ratio failures.

**Second demonstration of the structural finding logged yesterday, now with the tape moving against it.** `daily-summary` places a **canonical 10% trail** on every position (Rule 6, 36 placements, zero exceptions), so a **2:1** R:R mechanically requires a **+20% target** — which no sector ETF supports honestly, since there is no analyst range to anchor one. The consequence is that **`tier: core` adds are effectively only possible while Rule 5's relaxed 1.5:1 floor is armed, and Rule 5 only arms *after* the book has spent two sessions below the deployment floor.** Today sharpens it: XLF, the name this log has now wanted for three sessions, has risen **+2.2% since the entry it was refused at**, so the ratio deteriorates every day the trigger stays disarmed. **This is not a rule violation and was not overridden — it is a standing proposal for Friday's review, restated because the cost is now measurable rather than hypothetical.**

### Risk Factors
- **Macro — the binary moved to T+1 and the book is fully invested into it.** **July PCE + Q2 GDP Wed Aug 26 08:30 ET (T+1)**, then **Jackson Hole Thu Aug 27 (T+2)**, into a **75.06%-deployed** book with **no protection** and a **15.8 VIX** offering none cheaply. A hot PCE followed by a hawkish Powell is the adverse path and it hits **Real Estate (26.85% of deployed) hardest** — the most rate-sensitive sleeve in the book.
- **GILD carries an idiosyncratic binary on T+2, and it is the book's only satellite.** The **BIC/LEN PDUFA decision is Thursday Aug 27** — the same day Jackson Hole opens. GILD is $1,609.63 = 15.57% of equity, sits +1.40% above entry, and is protected by a 10% trail at $132.1515 (hwm $146.835). An adverse FDA outcome is a gap risk a trailing stop does not bound; the 10% trail bounds the *drift*, not the *gap*. **No action is available or warranted** — this routine places no orders, the position is aged and protected, and the correct handling is that midday and daily-summary see the outcome. **Recorded so Thursday's runs are not surprised by it.**
- **Technology is breaking down the day before NVIDIA reports, and the book has zero exposure in either direction.** XLK is the worst RS50 in the complex (−5.36pp) below a falling 50-DMA; WDC/MU/STX/AVGO are −10 to −21pp on RS50. **A beat costs the book relative alpha on a day SPY rallies; a miss protects it.** This is a `pass=0` consequence rather than a view, but it is real tracking error and it lands in the same 48 hours as PCE and Jackson Hole.
- **Concentration — Health Care at 45.52% of deployed remains the tightest single-sector bet of the phase**, expressed through two instruments (XLV core + GILD satellite) that share a policy and pipeline-sentiment shock — and **GILD's PDUFA is a live example of exactly that shared exposure**. Inside the 50% cap, deliberate, and sited where the measured RS is (XLV RS50 +10.13pp, GILD +13.59pp).
- **Rule 3 drift, thirteenth session:** **XLB 20.74%** and **XLRE 20.15%** of equity sit *through* the 20% per-position cap on appreciation. Not a breach — neither was bought through it — but neither can absorb a share, which is why screening must look for a *new* name rather than an add.
- **XLB is the softest core reading in the book.** RS50 fell +2.53 → **+1.24pp** in one session, the weakest of the four passing ETFs, on the book's largest unrealized gain (+7.03%) and its tightest trail (5%, stop $51.4805 vs last $53.58 — 3.9% of room). It is not Rule-16-flaggable (above entry, RS10 positive) but it is the position closest to a Rule 8 or Rule 16 event.

### Decision
**HOLD** — no orders. Fifth HOLD of the month, second consecutive, and the second driven purely by the R:R floor.
- **Zero ideas cleared the gate.** Core: 4 of 11 sector ETFs pass `rscreen`; **XLB and XLV are `floor_skip` on Rule 3**, and **XLE and XLF fail the 2:1 R:R floor** that `sizing.py redeploy` restored on a 75.06% deployment (`triggered: false`). Satellite: 13 of 23 names pass `rscreen` and **all 23 are screened out on `macro-window: PCE T+1 / Jackson Hole T+2`**, each also failing at least one independent gate.
- **The refusals are the same two as yesterday, and both got harder.** XLF is +2.2% above the entry it was refused at Friday; XLE would need an 8.1% mark-up of its own standing target. Declining to inflate a target to manufacture a ratio is the test that refused XLE, ABBV and LLY — applying it on the third consecutive day to the name this log would most like to own is the point.
- **The tape is on the book's side today.** Futures are lower on a technology-led selloff that the measured screen confirms independently (XLK worst RS50 in the complex, below a falling 50-DMA), and the book holds **zero Info Tech** with **24.94% cash**. Both are consequences of the screen, not calls — but on a red open they are the right consequences.
- **Nothing in the book needs action.** All 4 positions are above entry, all 108 shares carry armed GTC trails, deployment is in band at 75.06%, core is 79.26% of deployed, no sector exceeds 50%, and Rule 10 closes only Industrials and Consumer Staples — neither held.

### Risk Factors
- **Macro — the whole day is a coiled spring, and the coil is cheap.** VIX ~14.9 with the S&P flat into a **Chair keynote at T+1**. Low realized vol plus a scheduled binary is precisely the configuration where a hawkish tone repriced across the curve produces a 1.5–2% index day. The book is 68% deployed and 32% cash, which is accidentally the right posture for it — the cash is a Rule 5 deficiency and a keynote hedge at the same time.
- **Idiosyncratic, and today's largest — GILD BIC/LEN PDUFA at T+0.** A binary FDA decision on a **15.57%-of-equity satellite**, quoting **−1.66% pre-market ($145.63 vs $148.09)** before the news is out. Approval is the base case (priority review, virologically-suppressed label, bictegravir + lenacapavir single tablet), but a CRL or a restrictive label is a gap-risk event that **no stop can price** — the standing 10% trail (stop $134.66, hwm $149.62) is the correct and only mechanism, and it will fill below its trigger on a gap. **No action is available or appropriate: Rule 15 is not engaged (nothing opened today), and this routine never sells.** Sizing is the protection, and at 15.57% it is within the cap but is the single largest binary exposure in the book.
- **Sector — Health Care 49.94% of deployed, hovering on the 50% cap.** It crossed *through* the cap yesterday and slipped back under today only because GILD fell. The cap is forward-looking (Rule 12 does not force a sell), so this is a **gate, not a violation** — but the practical effect is that the sleeve with the second-best measured RS50 (+12.25pp) is unbuyable, and **the PDUFA outcome moves both legs of a half-the-book sector at once.**
- **Sector — Energy's YTD leadership is a decaying premium.** XLE's +43.1% and +11.45pp RS50 were built substantially on the Iran/Hormuz risk bid, which has unwound ~11% from the Aug 20 spike over two sessions. The RS screen reads the trailing move; it cannot read that the catalyst behind it reversed. Flagged so a future XLE idea is judged on the post-unwind tape, not the pre-unwind statistic.
- **Structural — deployment 68.14%, below the Rule 5 floor for a second session.** Cash drag was 0.7bp of yesterday's miss (near zero on a flat tape) but it compounds on any up day. The mechanical cause is honest — the XLB scale-out moved $698 to cash from a book already clinging to the floor by 13bp — but the screen has now admitted nothing for four sessions, so **there is no mechanism currently converting that cash back into exposure.** Restoring the floor needs ~$705; the only name with both Rule 3 room and a passing screen is XLB, and it fails R:R by a factor of seven.
- **Rule 10 — Industrials remains armed and closed** (FERG −$6.12 Aug 19 → XLI −$22.35 Aug 20). XLI's +16.0% YTD is not reachable.

### Decision
**HOLD — 0 ideas.** Patience > activity.

Every branch closed for a reason that is measured and logged: **satellites shut on a T+1 Chair keynote** (TRV the one screen-passer, refused on the window), **cores shut on a 2:1 floor that a mandated 10% stop makes unreachable from 200-day highs** (XLE/XLF/XLB/XLV all pass momentum, all fail arithmetic), **Health Care shut on the sector cap**, **Industrials shut on Rule 10**, **XLRE and XLV shut on Rule 3 room**. Week 18 stays at **0 of 5 buy slots used** — the weekly cap has still never bound in this phase, which is itself the finding.

`market-open` should short-circuit to STEP 7 with **0 orders**. The live questions are for the **weekly review tomorrow**, and they are now specific: (1) a 10% mandated stop plus a 2:1 floor is structurally incompatible with sector-ETF entries near 200-day highs — four consecutive shutout sessions is evidence, not noise, and Rule 5's 1.5:1 relaxation **provably does not fix it**; (2) the satellite sleeve has been macro-gated for four straight sessions on a single event, and the window clears Monday with TRV (+19.35pp RS50) queued.
